l-m-e6-b01-01.goal: Check whether the claim "the ratio wey get bigger first term get bigger ratio value too" dey always true, then find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-e6-b01-01.material: The ratio value of a:b na a÷b. Claim: when you compare two ratios, the one wey get bigger first term always get bigger ratio value. Find one case wey this claim wrong.

l-m-e6-b01-01.s.s1.explain: 6:20=0.3 and 3:4=0.75. The first term 6 big pass, but the ratio value small pass, so e be counterexample.
l-m-e6-b01-01.s.s2.model.0: The ratio value of 6:20 na 0.3 and that of 3:4 na 0.75. The first term 6 big pass but the ratio value small pass, so e be counterexample.

l-m-e6-b05-10.s.s1.r.a: With only two values, you no fit tell how the other records affect am.
l-m-e6-b05-10.s.s1.o.b: Sum of all records and number of records
l-m-e6-b05-10.s.s1.r.c: You no fit find the average from one record only.
l-m-e6-b05-10.s.s1.o.d: The record wey happen most often
l-m-e6-b05-10.s.s1.r.d: The value wey show most often different from average.
l-m-e6-b05-10.s.s1.explain: Average na sum of all the records divided by number of records.
l-m-e6-b05-10.s.s2.model.0: Average na sum divided by number of records, so you need sum of all the records and number of records.
l-m-e6-b05-10.s.s2.model.1: If you only get highest and lowest records, you no know the rest, so you no fit find average. That why you need the sum and number of records.

l-m-e6-b05-34.goal: Work out which standard (information) you must get to find the price of 7 candies, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-e6-b05-34.material: 3 candies cost 1,500 won. Think about which information you must get to find the price of 7 candies with proportion.

l-m-e6-b05-34.s.s2.model.0: Even if the number dey grow, the price of one must remain the same, so you must get this information. Then 500×7=3,500 won.

l-m-e6-b01-11.title: Wetin go happen to di sum if we keep adding halves?
l-m-e6-b01-11.goal: Look plenty examples of sums wey start from 1/2 and keep adding half of di previous amount, talk di pattern, and check am with one new case.
l-m-e6-b01-11.material: 1/2, 1/2+1/4=3/4, 1/2+1/4+1/8=7/8, 1/2+1/4+1/8+1/16=15/16. Find di pattern for how di denominator and numerator of di sum dey change when we keep adding half.
l-m-e6-b01-11.s.s1.prompt: If you use di pattern, wetin be di sum of 1/2+1/4+1/8+1/16+1/32?
l-m-e6-b01-11.s.s1.r.b: E be di same as 15/16. We still need add 1/32.
l-m-e6-b01-11.s.s1.r.c: Di denominator go up by just 1. Di denominator dey double every time (×2).
l-m-e6-b01-11.s.s1.r.d: Di numerator big by 1 too much. Di sum no become 1.
l-m-e6-b01-11.s.s1.explain: Di sum na fraction wey im numerator small pass im denominator by 1. Di denominator na 32, so e be 31/32.
l-m-e6-b01-11.s.s2.model.0: Di sums 1/2, 3/4, 7/8, 15/16 each get numerator wey small pass di denominator by 1, so with denominator 32 e be 31/32.
l-m-e6-b01-11.s.s2.model.1: If you add 1/32 to 15/16, e give 30/32+1/32=31/32, so di pattern correct.

l-m-e6-b01-12.goal: Look plenty examples of multiplying 99 by natural number, talk di pattern, and check am with one new case.

l-m-e6-b01-12.s.s1.prompt: If you use di pattern, wetin be di value of 99×7?
l-m-e6-b01-12.s.s1.r.a: Dis na di value of 99×8. Check di number wey dem dey multiply.
l-m-e6-b01-12.s.s1.r.b: Dem calculate am as 100×7. 99 small pass 100 by 1.
l-m-e6-b01-12.s.s1.r.d: Dem only subtract 3 from 700. We must subtract di multiplier 7.
l-m-e6-b01-12.s.s1.explain: Di product na 100×(di multiplier) minus di multiplier. 700−7=693.
l-m-e6-b01-12.s.s2.model.0: 198=200−2 and 297=300−3, so we subtract di multiplier from 100×(di multiplier). 700−7=693.
l-m-e6-b01-12.s.s2.model.1: 99 small pass 100 by 1, so we subtract 7 from 100×7=700 and we get 693.

l-m-e6-b01-13.s.s1.r.a: Dem move di decimal point go di wrong place.

l-m-e6-b01-13.s.s2.model.1: 0.25 enter 1 four times (4), so to divide number by 0.25 make am 4 times as big. So 5÷0.25=20.

l-m-e6-b01-15.goal: Look plenty examples of di relation between prices before and after 10% discount, talk di pattern, and check am with one new case.
l-m-e6-b01-15.material: Prices before and after 10% discount na 1000 won→900 won, 2000 won→1800 won, 3000 won→2700 won. Find di pattern between di price before and after di discount.
l-m-e6-b01-15.s.s1.prompt: If di price after di discount na 6300 won, wetin be di price before di discount?
l-m-e6-b01-15.s.s1.r.a: Dem add 1000 won. Di price dey change in proportion.
l-m-e6-b01-15.s.s1.r.c: Dem add 10% to 6300. We must divide by 0.9.
l-m-e6-b01-15.s.s1.r.d: Dem multiply 6300 by 0.9 again. To go backward, we must divide.
l-m-e6-b01-15.s.s1.explain: Di price after di discount na 0.9 times di original. 6300÷0.9=7000, so e be 7000 won.
l-m-e6-b01-15.s.s2.model.0: 900÷1000 and 1800÷2000 both na 0.9, so di price after di discount na 0.9 times di original. 6300÷0.9=7000.
l-m-e6-b01-15.s.s2.model.1: 90% of 7000 won na 6300 won, so di price before di discount na 7000 won.

l-m-e6-b02-11.goal: Find and talk one rule from several examples of how to divide two fractions wey get di same denominator, then check dat rule with new case.
l-m-e6-b02-11.material: 6/7÷2/7=3, 8/9÷4/9=2, and 9/10÷3/10=3. Find di rule for how dem dey decide di quotient wen you divide two fractions wey get di same denominator.
l-m-e6-b02-11.s.s1.prompt: If you use di rule, wetin be di value of 12/13÷3/13?

l-m-e6-b02-11.s.s1.r.b: Dis one multiply di fractions. You must no multiply inside division.
l-m-e6-b02-11.s.s1.r.c: Dis one keep di denominator inside di quotient. Di denominators cancel out.
l-m-e6-b02-11.s.s1.explain: Wen di denominators na di same, divide di numerators. 12÷3=4, so 12/13÷3/13=4.
l-m-e6-b02-11.s.s2.model.0: Like 6÷2=3, 8÷4=2, and 9÷3=3, di quotient na di value wey you get wen you divide di numerators, so 12÷3=4.
l-m-e6-b02-11.s.s2.model.1: Wen di denominators na di same, e be di same as to group 12 pieces wey get di same size into groups of 3, so di quotient na 4.

l-m-e6-b01-26.title: To change the ratio 9:25 to percent
l-m-e6-b01-26.goal: Change the percent wey show the ratio 9:25 go another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e6-b01-26.material: The ratio value of the ratio 9:25 na 9÷25. Dem fit show ratio value as decimal or fraction, and if you multiply by 100 e go turn percent. Change the same size to percent.
l-m-e6-b01-26.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be the ratio 9:25 as percent?
l-m-e6-b01-26.s.s1.r.a: Dem join 9 and 25 together and read am like decimal.
l-m-e6-b01-26.s.s1.r.b: Dem mistake the difference 25−9 for the ratio value.
l-m-e6-b01-26.s.s1.r.c: Dem calculate 25÷9. We must divide the first term by the second term.
l-m-e6-b01-26.s.s1.explain: 9÷25=0.36, so if you multiply by 100 e go give 36%.
l-m-e6-b01-26.s.s2.model.0: 9÷25=0.36, and if you multiply 0.36 by 100 e go give 36, so e be 36%.
l-m-e6-b01-26.s.s2.model.1: 9:25 na 9 out of 25 squares, and if you stretch am to 100 squares e go be 36 squares, so e be 36%.

l-m-e6-b01-27.title: To talk 0.6×0.5 with words
l-m-e6-b01-27.goal: Change the meaning of the multiplication 0.6×0.5 go another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e6-b01-27.material: Make we talk the multiplication 0.6×0.5 with words. To multiply number by decimal mean say you dey find some times (or some part) of that number.
l-m-e6-b01-27.s.s1.prompt: Which words mean the same thing as 0.6×0.5?
l-m-e6-b01-27.s.s1.r.a: To multiply by 0.5 dey make am half, no be 2 times.
l-m-e6-b01-27.s.s1.o.b: Di number wey you get wen you add 0.5 to 0.6
l-m-e6-b01-27.s.s1.o.c: Di number wey you get wen you divide 0.6 by 0.5
l-m-e6-b01-27.s.s1.r.c: To multiply by 0.5 and to divide by 0.5 different.
l-m-e6-b01-27.s.s1.explain: 0.5 na half. 0.6×0.5 na half of 0.6, wey be 0.3.
l-m-e6-b01-27.s.s2.model.0: 0.5 na half of 1, so if you multiply 0.6 by 0.5 e give half of 0.6. If you calculate am, e be 0.3.
l-m-e6-b01-27.s.s2.model.1: To take 0.5 times 0.6 mean say you cut am for half, so e be di same as half of 0.6.

l-m-e6-b01-28.title: To change 5:3 to ratio value of di whole
l-m-e6-b01-28.goal: Change di ratio of blue pens to black pens to ratio value of di whole, for another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-e6-b01-28.material: One pencil holder get blue pens and black pens for ratio 5:3. Change di ratio of di two kinds to di ratio value of black pens inside di whole.
l-m-e6-b01-28.s.s1.prompt: How much of di whole na black pens?
l-m-e6-b01-28.s.s1.r.a: Na di ratio value of di number of black pens to di number of blue pens be dat. Di whole no be di base.
l-m-e6-b01-28.s.s1.r.c: Na di ratio value of di blue pens inside di whole be dat.
l-m-e6-b01-28.s.s1.r.d: Na di whole wey dem divide by di black pens. Dem write am di wrong way round.
l-m-e6-b01-28.s.s1.explain: Di total na 5+3=8, and 3 of dem na black pens. Di black pens na 3/8 of di total.
l-m-e6-b01-28.s.s2.model.0: If you add 5 blue pens and 3 black pens, di total na 8, so di black pens na 3/8 of di total.
l-m-e6-b01-28.s.s2.model.1: If you split di whole into 8 parts, di black pens take 3 parts, so you fit rewrite am as 3/8.

l-m-e6-b01-29.title: To change circumference to formula for di diameter
l-m-e6-b01-29.goal: Rewrite di formula to find di diameter from di circumference for another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-e6-b01-29.material: Di circumference na di diameter × pi (3.14). Wen di distance around circle na 31.4 cm, reverse dis relationship to make formula for di diameter.
l-m-e6-b01-29.s.s1.prompt: Which one na di correct formula to find di diameter?
l-m-e6-b01-29.s.s1.r.a: Dis one multiply di circumference by pi. You go find di diameter if you divide di circumference by pi.
l-m-e6-b01-29.s.s1.r.b: Na di formula for di radius be dis, no be di diameter.
l-m-e6-b01-29.s.s1.r.c: Dis one use subtraction. If you reverse multiplication relationship, e give division.
l-m-e6-b01-29.s.s1.explain: Since circumference = diameter × 3.14, diameter = circumference ÷ 3.14. Since 31.4÷3.14=10, e be 10 cm.
l-m-e6-b01-29.s.s2.model.0: Because di reverse of multiplication na division, di diameter na di circumference wey you divide by pi: 31.4÷3.14=10.
l-m-e6-b01-29.s.s2.model.1: If you multiply di diameter by 3.14, e give 31.4, so if you divide 31.4 by 3.14, e give diameter of 10 cm.

l-m-e6-b01-30.title: To talk 25% as number of people
l-m-e6-b01-30.goal: Rewrite di 25% wey choose "like" for survey for another form (formula, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-e6-b01-30.material: For one survey, 25% of di people choose "like." 25% mean 25 out of 100 and e equal 1/4 of di whole. Make we talk di same thing as number of people.
l-m-e6-b01-30.s.s1.prompt: Which statement mean di same thing as 25%?

l-m-e6-b01-30.s.s2.model.0: 25% na 25/100, and if you simplify am e give 1/4, so e mean di same thing as to talk say 1 out of 4 people.
l-m-e6-b01-30.s.s2.model.1: If you divide di whole equally into 4, one share na 25%, so e mean di same thing as 1 out of 4 people.

l-m-e6-b02-26.title: How to talk pie chart with words
l-m-e6-b02-26.goal: Change the data for pie chart, A 50%, B 25%, C 25%, to another form (expression, table, picture, or words) and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e6-b02-26.material: For the pie chart, A na 50%, B na 25%, and C na 25%. Make we talk with words wetin this graph dey show.
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s1.prompt: Which statement mean the same thing as the graph?
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s1.o.a: C na half of the whole
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s1.r.a: C na 25%, wey be 1/4 of the whole.
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s1.r.b: B na 25% and A na 50%. A na 2 times B.
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s1.o.c: A equal B and C put together
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s1.r.d: A big pass B. B na half of A.
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s1.explain: B and C together make 25%+25%=50%, wey equal A.
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s2.model.0: B plus C na 25+25=50, so we fit say e equal A.
l-m-e6-b02-26.s.s2.model.1: A na half of the whole, and B and C share the other half equally, so A equal the sum of B and C.

l-m-e6-b02-27.title: 60 km for one hour, say am another way
l-m-e6-b02-27.goal: Change the speed of going 60 km for one hour to another form (expression, table, picture, or words) and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e6-b02-27.material: One car dey go 60 km for one hour with the same speed. Make we show the same speed another way by changing the time and the distance.
l-m-e6-b02-27.s.s1.prompt: Which statement show the same speed?
l-m-e6-b02-27.s.s1.r.a: If dem cut the time to half, the distance go cut to half too.
l-m-e6-b02-27.s.s1.r.b: For 1 minute, e dey go 1 km, no be 6 km.
l-m-e6-b02-27.s.s1.r.c: If the time become 2 times as long, the distance go become 2 times as long too.
l-m-e6-b02-27.s.s1.explain: E dey go 60 km for one hour (60 minutes), so for 30 minutes e go go half of that, 30 km.
l-m-e6-b02-27.s.s2.model.0: E dey go 60 km for one hour, so for 30 minutes e go go half, 30 km, wey be the same speed.
l-m-e6-b02-27.s.s2.model.1: If dem cut the time to half, the distance wey e travel go cut to half too, so 30 km for 30 minutes mean the same thing.

l-m-e6-b02-28.title: Write 0.6:0.9 as ratio of simple whole numbers
l-m-e6-b02-28.goal: Change the decimal ratio 0.6:0.9 to another form (expression, table, picture, or words) and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e6-b02-28.material: The ratio 0.6:0.9 na ratio wey dem write with decimals. The ratio no dey change if you multiply or divide the first term and the second term by the same number. Make we write the same ratio as the simplest ratio of whole numbers.
l-m-e6-b02-28.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be the simplest ratio of whole numbers wey equal 0.6:0.9?
l-m-e6-b02-28.s.s1.r.a: E na the same ratio, but you fit divide am by 3 make e simple pass.
l-m-e6-b02-28.s.s1.r.b: E na the same ratio, but whole numbers no make am.
l-m-e6-b02-28.s.s1.r.c: You write the terms the wrong order. 0.6 suppose come first.
l-m-e6-b02-28.s.s1.explain: If you multiply 0.6:0.9 by 10 e go be 6:9, and if you divide by 3 e go be 2:3.
l-m-e6-b02-28.s.s2.model.0: If you multiply by 10 e go be 6:9, and if you divide the two terms by 3 e go be 2:3, wey be the simplest ratio.
l-m-e6-b02-28.s.s2.model.1: 0.6 na 2 times 0.3 and 0.9 na 3 times 0.3, so the ratio na 2:3.

l-m-e6-b02-29.title: Write surface area as expression
l-m-e6-b02-29.goal: Change the expression for the surface area of a rectangular prism to another form (expression, table, picture, or words) and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e6-b02-29.material: One rectangular prism dey wey long 3 cm, wide 4 cm, and tall 5 cm. A rectangular prism get three pairs of faces wey be the same. Make we turn this one to expression to find the surface area.
l-m-e6-b02-29.s.s1.prompt: Which expression give the surface area correct?
l-m-e6-b02-29.s.s1.r.a: You add only one face from each of the 3 pairs. You suppose multiply by 2.
l-m-e6-b02-29.s.s1.r.c: You add only the lengths and multiply by 2. You suppose add the areas of the faces.
l-m-e6-b02-29.s.s1.r.d: This one na the expression for the volume.
l-m-e6-b02-29.s.s1.explain: The areas of the three pairs of faces na 12, 20, and 15. Two dey for each one, so 2×47=94 cm².
l-m-e6-b02-29.s.s2.model.0: Three pairs of faces dey and the faces for each pair get the same area, so multiply the sum of one face from each pair, 47, by 2 to get 94.
l-m-e6-b02-29.s.s2.model.1: Two faces dey for top and bottom, front and back, and left and right, so we fit write am as 2×(3×4+4×5+3×5).

l-m-e6-b02-30.goal: Say 1.25 hours for hours and minutes, and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e6-b02-30.material: You do exercise for 1.25 hours. 1 hour na 60 minutes. Make we talk the same length of time by splitting am to 'hours' and 'minutes'.
l-m-e6-b02-30.s.s1.prompt: How many hours and minutes be 1.25 hours?

l-m-e6-b02-30.s.s1.r.b: You move the decimal point of 0.25. 0.25 hours na 15 minutes.
l-m-e6-b02-30.s.s1.r.c: You read the decimal 0.25 as 25 minutes. 0.25 hours na 1/4 of 60 minutes.

l-m-e6-b02-30.s.s2.model.1: 0.25×60=15, so 0.25 hours na 15 minutes. So e na 1 hour 15 minutes.

l-m-e6-b01-31.s.s2.model.1: Di more di sides na di same size, di fewer faces go show for outside, so 2×3×4 get smaller surface area than 1×4×6.

l-m-e6-b02-32.goal: Compare two ways to estimate 3.4+3.4+3.4, choose di one wey better, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-e6-b02-32.material: Estimate di sum of 3.4+3.4+3.4 to di ones place. One person round each number first and talk say 3+3+3=9, and another person find 3.4×3=10.2 and talk say 10. Di exact sum na 10.2.
l-m-e6-b02-32.s.s1.prompt: Which way close pass to di exact sum, and why?
l-m-e6-b02-32.s.s1.o.a: Round after we add: because 10 near 10.2
l-m-e6-b02-32.s.s1.o.c: Round each number: because e easy to calculate and e always dey correct
l-m-e6-b02-32.s.s1.r.c: Because something easy no mean say e dey more correct.

l-m-e6-b02-32.s.s1.r.d: Di differences no be di same: dem be 1.2 and 0.2.
